_doc: Scale versus count: the precision cost of relaxing _is_scale_question.
Widening the range check so 0-based scales are recognised also pulls count
variables in, because a 0-4 count of children and a 0-4 Likert item have
identical value distributions. This fixture holds both directions so the
trade-off is measurable rather than assumed.
`expected` records CURRENT behaviour (the unfixed detector). It is a guard
rail for the pending fix, not a statement that current behaviour is right:
the scale rows marked `numeric` are exactly the defect being fixed.
Update `expected` together with the fix and record the new trade-off
Data is generated deterministically from (low, high, seed); 300 rows.
The `ambiguous` group is the point of the whole exercise: those columns are
undecidable from values alone. No detector setting can resolve them.

scales.defect: NPS, the most common 0-10 scale there is

ambiguous.name: Q12
ambiguous.why: Could be a 5-point scale or a count of children. Values are identical; the name carries no signal. Undecidable without a schema.

ambiguous.name: item_3
ambiguous.why: Could be NPS or a count of purchases. Undecidable without a schema.

ambiguous.name: v7
ambiguous.why: Currently read as a scale, but could equally be a count of rooms. The verdict here is a coin flip that happens to land on scale.
